title: HTTP ingress trace propagation rewrite + Tempo outbound shim for legacy clients
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: Our HTTP ingress receives traces from a mix of modern OpenTelemetry SDKs and a number of legacy/3rd-party clients that use nonstandard trace headers (X-Request-ID variants, legacy b3 single-header formats, and a truncated trace-id). Downstream the collector currently forwards OTLP faithfully to Tempo, but Tempo ingestion expects full 128-bit trace IDs and certain resource attributes (service.name, environment, deployment). This mismatch causes partial traces, misattributed spans, and broken waterfall views for customers.

Goal: Implement a lightweight HTTP ingress layer that: 1) normalizes and rewrites incoming trace propagation headers into a consistent W3C TraceContext (traceparent) where possible; 2) synthesizes or expands short trace IDs to 128-bit deterministic values without breaking dedup semantics; 3) enriches OTLP spans with mapped resource attributes; and 4) provides a small Tempo outbound shim that applies minimal schema-mapping so Tempo receives well-formed spans even when the upstream sdk is old. The shim should be safe for high-throughput ingress (target <5% p95 latency increase) and pluggable behind our existing otlp-relay pipeline.

Constraints and non-goals: We will not reimplement sampling policies here. This ticket focuses on header translation, ID normalization, and attribute mapping. Full adaptive sampling and tenant-aware heuristics remain separate. We also avoid persistent buffering; only in-memory bounded buffers with backpressure will be used to avoid data loss at scale.

Why now: Several enterprise customers reported broken trace views when using our hosted ingress in front of legacy services. SREs have manually patched spans in dashboards which is unsustainable. Providing a compatibility shim reduces customer support load and improves trace fidelity across the platform.
tasks: Design header translation table for: B3 single, B3 multi, X-Request-ID variants, Jaeger-uber-trace-id -> traceparent
Implement Rust-based ingress middleware to parse and rewrite headers (reuse existing ingress codepath where possible)
Create deterministic expansion routine for 64-bit trace ids (high-entropy prefix + existing lower bits) and record provenance tag
Map legacy resource attributes to standard OTLP resource labels (service.name, service.version, deployment.environment)
Build Tempo outbound shim: minimal protobuf mapping and span checksum to avoid duplicates
Add unit + integration tests with synthetic legacy clients and real sample traces
Run load test (k6) to validate latency and CPU impact; target p95 ingress latency increase <5%
Prepare rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics + rollback triggers
acceptance_criteria: Incoming B3 single-header and X-Request-ID traces are visible as single cohesive traces in Tempo instead of fragmented spans
Trace IDs expanded deterministically for short IDs and an attribute 'trace.redwood.id_expanded' set to 'true' for visibility
No customer-visible increase in trace duplication in Tempo (duplicate rate delta < 0.1%)
P95 ingress latency degradation under realistic load <5% and CPU delta under 10%
Canary rollout document and runbook validated; automatic rollback triggers defined (error-rate increase > 2x or trace-loss > 0.5%)
notes: Trade-offs: Deterministic expansion risks collision if two different 64-bit ids collide with same expansion scheme; mitigation: include provenance tag (client-id or ingress-timestamp) when available and prefer high-entropy prefix from remote IP/tenant salt.
Decision: Use W3C traceparent as canonical internal propagation format to simplify downstream mapping and support modern SDKs.
Alternative considered: enrich spans downstream in Tempo via ingest pipeline transforms. Rejected due to inability to fix header-less propagation between services at ingress boundary.

Security: ensure trace normalization does not leak sensitive attributes. Attribute mapping list will be whitelisted; no raw headers will be forwarded to logs except in debug builds behind feature flag.
Implementation language: ingress middleware in Rust to match current high-performance path; Tempo shim as a light protobuf translator (Rust or Go lib depending on team availability).
